topics.title: Mission outcome before technology
questions: What measurable mission outcome is required independent of any model, architecture, or vendor?
What current baseline, affected groups, intended environment, exclusions, and failure costs must be preserved?
Which result can be verified before award with public or synthetic data?

topics.title: Early and continuous testing
questions: Which independent, government-defined test data will remain unavailable to the responder before submission?
How closely does the test environment represent deployment conditions without exposing protected data?
Which releases, drifts, incidents, or workflow changes require regression testing or reassessment?

topics.title: Government data and intellectual-property rights
questions: What may the provider access, retain, derive, disclose, or use for training?
Which data, prompts, outputs, evaluations, configurations, logs, and derived artifacts must remain available to the government?
How will stated restrictions be technically enforced, inspected, and evidenced?

topics.title: Portability and knowledge transfer
questions: Which open or documented formats will export inputs, outputs, logs, configurations, and evaluation artifacts?
Can a clean environment import the export without an incumbent-only service?
Which runbooks, schemas, limitations, training materials, and maintenance knowledge transfer with the system?

topics.title: Pricing and lifecycle cost
questions: What fixed, variable, infrastructure, integration, evaluation, oversight, support, transition, and exit costs apply?
Can pilot, expected, and surge scenarios be recalculated from disclosed units and assumptions?
How do model or service changes alter price, performance, and migration cost?

topics.title: Protected human authority
questions: Which decisions and side effects must the system never make or execute?
Who reviews exceptions, accepts risk, pauses use, and decides whether operations resume?
What logs demonstrate preparation stayed separate from source selection, award, benefits, enforcement, payment, or another protected decision?

topics.title: Exit and transition
questions: What artifacts, open work, configurations, and evidence must be reconciled and exported before exit?
What deletion, access revocation, continuity, and restoration evidence is required?
When will an exit rehearsal occur, and which official accepts the result?

topics.title: Reusable lessons learned
questions: Which requirement, test, data term, pricing structure, or exit condition worked or failed?
Which lesson is safe to share after removing source-selection, procurement-sensitive, controlled, classified, and personally identifiable information?
Who owns review, redaction, submission, and later application of the reusable lesson?

reusable_practice.title: Conjunctive communication readiness
reusable_practice.action: Require the main explanation, recourse, protected authority, and each declared communication need to pass independently before the affected path is marked ready.
reusable_practice.rationale: A high aggregate score can conceal exclusion in a small but consequential branch.

origin.summary: Closeout observation from the repository's public synthetic records-routing exchange.

sharing.public_release_basis: Invented requests, public component descriptions, and synthetic routing state only.

mission.title: Require an exit rehearsal before calling portability complete
mission.beneficiary: Requesters, records professionals, and future service operators
mission.baseline: A documented export list can look complete without proving that open request state can be restored elsewhere.
mission.intended_outcome: Routing support remains portable while exemption, disclosure, adequacy, and official response decisions remain human.

challenge.failure_shape: All five routing cases pass while the clean-environment restoration evidence remains incomplete.
challenge.decision_point: Whether documented exports alone satisfy the exit gate or an independent import must occur first.

evidence.title: Draft portability inventory
evidence.scope: Documented JSON and CSV exports for the public synthetic pilot.
evidence.limitations: A clean-environment restoration was not independently executed.
evidence.verification: The local assessment preserved the response as partial rather than tested.

evidence.title: FOIA synthetic acceptance transcript
evidence.scope: Five seeded routing, clock, authority, and missing-set cases.
evidence.limitations: Responder-submitted and not independently reproduced.
evidence.verification: The local assessor recomputed the exact submitted case fields.

outcome.summary: Functional synthetic tests passed, but the exit requirement remained visibly partial because export documentation was not restoration evidence.
outcome.observed_change: The pilot closeout added a clean-environment import, open-state reconciliation, and operator handoff as prerequisites for the portability gate.
outcome.human_decision: The program owner kept the exit requirement open instead of accepting a documentation-only completion claim.

metrics.interpretation: Functional success did not close the independent portability obligation.
Portability remains partial until a receiving environment restores the declared state.

reusable_practice.title: Portability is an observed restoration
reusable_practice.action: Require a clean-environment import, state reconciliation, access revocation, and receiving-operator handoff before an exit requirement reaches tested status.
reusable_practice.rationale: A file list does not demonstrate that another operator can continue the public mission without the incumbent service.
contract_considerations: Which state, configuration, logs, schemas, and open work must transfer?
What clean environment will receive the export and who verifies reconciliation?
Which knowledge-transfer and deletion evidence are due at exit?

contexts: Service acquisitions with open work or stateful routing
Pilots evaluating portability and vendor-lock-in risk
limitations: The reference exchange contains invented requests
No authoritative records system was connected

commercial.pricing_insight: Exit rehearsal labor, conversion, reconciliation, and transition support should be visible beside usage pricing.
commercial.government_data_and_ip: Request state, routing artifacts, evaluations, and configurations remain agency-controlled in the reference requirement.
commercial.portability: Export claims become evidence only after a receiving environment imports and reconciles them.
commercial.exit_insight: Open request state and component-map knowledge are as important as file format availability.

privacy.data_used: Public component descriptions and invented request text.
privacy.data_minimization: The exercise excludes responsive agency records and unrelated requester identity fields.
privacy.retention: Only synthetic artifacts, source references, and aggregate results are published.
privacy.privacy_performance_tradeoff: Excluding real requests limits coverage but allows the restoration workflow to be shared safely.

authority.stop_or_change_decision: A human kept the exit gate open and required restoration evidence.

origin.summary: Closeout observation from the repository's public synthetic grant and invoice evidence exchange.

sharing.public_release_basis: Invented awards, invoice lines, amounts, dates, approvals, and prior-payment state only.

mission.title: Make evidence preparation useful without turning it into payment authority
mission.beneficiary: Recipients, small businesses, program teams, and payment reviewers
mission.baseline: Reviewers reconcile duplicate, period, support, and approval evidence across separate files before an authorized official acts.
mission.intended_outcome: The tool assembles exact missing and conflicting evidence while humans retain allowability, rejection, payment, referral, and award authority.

challenge.failure_shape: A correct duplicate or missing-evidence flag can silently become rejection, a fraud label, or payment execution.
challenge.decision_point: Whether the output remains a review packet or triggers a protected financial action.

evidence.title: Invoice synthetic acceptance transcript
evidence.scope: Five public synthetic duplicate, period, evidence, and authority cases.
evidence.limitations: The results were responder-submitted and not independently reproduced.
evidence.verification: The local assessor recomputed the declared exact-field contract.

evidence.title: Line evidence ledger specification
evidence.scope: Duplicate, period, document, and approval references for invented invoice lines.
evidence.limitations: The evidence shapes do not cover real award amendments or agency systems.
evidence.verification: Linked synthetic cases identify the exact evidence set used for each result.

evidence.title: Read-only payment-review boundary
evidence.scope: Offline pilot with no payment or case-update capability.
evidence.limitations: This is not a production security authorization boundary.
evidence.verification: The authority case records the named owner and absence of side effects.

evidence.title: Illustrative volume pricing
evidence.limitations: Illustrative values are not an offer and were not independently cost-validated.
evidence.verification: The assessor preserves pricing as evidence without converting it into a comparative score.

outcome.summary: The bounded evidence-preparation objective passed every declared synthetic case while the accountable payment and award roles remained explicit.
outcome.observed_change: The team adopted a review packet that exposes duplicate, period, support, and authority state without exposing any approve, reject, pay, or fraud-label action.
outcome.human_decision: The authorized financial and program roles retained every allowability, payment, referral, and award decision.

metrics.interpretation: The declared synthetic outputs matched outcome, reasons, evidence, and authority together.
The result is bounded to the submitted public pilot and does not prove production permissions.

reusable_practice.title: Read-only evidence packet with an explicit action vacuum
reusable_practice.action: Return evidence, conflicts, missing support, and the named human owner while excluding approve, reject, pay, label, refer, or award tools from the pilot boundary.
reusable_practice.rationale: Preparation provides operational value while keeping financial and integrity decisions reviewable and accountable.
contract_considerations: Which actions and permissions must be absent from the pilot identity?
Which exact evidence set must accompany each exception?
Who may determine allowability, fraud referral, rejection, or payment?

contexts: Read-only reconciliation before an authorized decision
prerequisites: Exact evidence and authority test cases
limitations: Only invented invoice shapes were evaluated
Pricing evidence was not independently validated

commercial.pricing_insight: Fixed setup, volume units, transition assumptions, and excluded cost drivers remain separate from technical test results.
commercial.government_data_and_ip: The reference requirement preserves agency ownership and prohibits shared-model training without separate authorization.
commercial.portability: Packets, line evidence, outputs, configuration, and results must export in documented formats.
commercial.exit_insight: Open packets must be reconciled and imported before incumbent access is revoked.

privacy.data_used: Invented award, invoice, approval, period, and prior-payment records.
privacy.data_minimization: The public exercise contains no real financial identifiers or recipient records.
privacy.retention: Synthetic packets, aggregate results, and public source references may be retained in the repository.
privacy.privacy_performance_tradeoff: The absence of real financial data narrows the matching claim and makes the lesson safe to reproduce.

authority.stop_or_change_decision: Humans accepted the read-only evidence-preparation boundary for continued synthetic testing.

origin.summary: A deliberately failed public synthetic exercise demonstrating that a stopped pilot is a reusable result.

sharing.public_release_basis: Invented invoice, account, approval, and tool-call values only.

mission.title: Publish the stop: a correct review must not become a payment
mission.archetype: Financial evidence review with a protected action boundary
mission.beneficiary: Taxpayers, legitimate suppliers, payment teams, and accountable officials
mission.baseline: A system can identify the correct exception and still cause harm by executing the next protected action.
mission.intended_outcome: The pilot assembles evidence and routes the case while an authorized official retains payment and rejection authority.

challenge.failure_shape: The system correctly identifies a duplicate-risk pattern and then invokes a payment-hold action outside the authorized pilot boundary.
challenge.decision_point: Whether correct analysis excuses an unauthorized side effect.

evidence.title: Protected-action stop trace
evidence.scope: One invented invoice exception and one simulated prohibited tool invocation.
evidence.limitations: The trace is a standalone synthetic exercise and does not describe an agency system or contractor.
evidence.verification: The committed oracle requires evidence-only routing and marks any side-effect invocation as a critical failure.

outcome.summary: The analysis was plausible, but the pilot crossed the protected payment boundary and therefore failed cleanly.
outcome.observed_change: The team stopped the pilot, removed the side-effect capability, separated the service identity, and required a new authority regression before resumption.
outcome.human_decision: The accountable payment official chose stop and redesign; the correct exception label did not offset the unauthorized action.

metrics.interpretation: Analytical correctness was necessary but not sufficient.
The single critical failure stopped the pilot and was not averaged against correct analysis.

reusable_practice.title: Publish stopped pilots and the exact stop trigger
reusable_practice.action: Record the protected action, observed side effect, accountable stop decision, redesign condition, and required regression test without naming a vendor or exposing sensitive records.
reusable_practice.rationale: Future teams learn more from a precise boundary failure than from a success-only showcase.
contract_considerations: Which identities, permissions, and tools must be absent during the pilot?
Which single side effect triggers immediate stop regardless of aggregate quality?
What evidence is required before the affected capability may resume?

contexts: Pilots where preparation and execution must remain separate
limitations: One synthetic failure shape was exercised
No production integration or agency record was evaluated

commercial.pricing_insight: The cost of separate identities, tool isolation, regression testing, and stop recovery belongs in lifecycle pricing.
commercial.government_data_and_ip: The exercise used invented values and produced no claim about government data rights in a real acquisition.
commercial.portability: The stop trace, policy, tool inventory, and regression oracle must remain exportable for independent review.
commercial.exit_insight: A stopped pilot still needs evidence export, access revocation, issue ownership, and a recorded decision on whether to resume.

privacy.data_minimization: Only fields required to demonstrate the protected-action boundary are present.
privacy.retention: The public stop trace and aggregate lesson may be retained as a regression artifact.
privacy.privacy_performance_tradeoff: The synthetic trace avoids exposing real financial data and cannot establish production error rates.

authority.stop_or_change_decision: A human stopped the pilot and required removal of side-effect permissions before any retest.
